content.title: The MDMA / SEA-IT Study
content.summary: A clinical study comparing two intensive treatments for military-related PTSD: MDMA-assisted therapy and SEA-IT.
content.description:
Many veterans suffer from PTSD symptoms along with other psychological difficulties related to experiences they went through or witnessed during their military service.

The current study offers two intensive treatments:

- **One treatment** is MDMA-assisted therapy, which combines taking the psychedelic substance with tailored psychotherapy.
- **The second treatment** is SEA-IT (Somatic Experiential Acceptance Intensive Trauma focused Therapy), an intensive therapy focused on the body, experience and acceptance, based on a psychedelic model.

The study seeks to examine the ways in which the treatments affect various psychological and neuropsychological aspects, and to understand the mechanism of intensive treatment.

Eligibility for the study is based on an assessment process and does not allow a choice between the treatments.
content.population: People living with military-related PTSD who have had previous trauma-focused therapy and whose symptoms persist
eligibility: Living with military trauma or PTSD
Has previously taken part in trauma-focused therapy, but symptoms persist
Able to commit to an intensive process of 3-3.5 months (16 sessions, in Jerusalem)
team: Under the supervision of Prof. Pinchas Dannon, Head of Psychiatry at Herzog Hospital

content.title: The SE PE Study
content.summary: A comparative study of Somatic Experiencing (SE) and prolonged exposure (PE) in treating military PTSD, provided free of charge across Israel.
content.description:
A comparative study of two treatment methods for PTSD: Somatic Experiencing (SE) compared with prolonged exposure (PE). The study was conducted over different periods - the COVID pandemic, a lull and war - and gives a broad picture of coping with PTSD in Israel in a changing reality.

As part of the program, free treatment is provided across Israel to people living with PTSD from their military service (veterans only, not those in regular service). Treatment is given with one of the two methods by certified therapists, and is accompanied by questionnaires, clinical assessments and follow-up by Metiv. The data is used for clinical research.
content.population: Veterans (not in regular service) living with PTSD from their military service

content.title: Combat Soldiers with PTSD Study
content.summary: A qualitative study on the experience of returning to combat in the Iron Swords war among combat soldiers who were living with military PTSD before the war.
content.description:
A qualitative study: analysis of interviews with combat soldiers called up for reserve duty who had a history of living with PTSD. A longitudinal study during the Iron Swords war.

The study includes an open interview with combat soldiers who took part in the war, in an attempt to understand their story, the complexity and how they coped.
content.population: Combat reservists who were living with military PTSD before the Iron Swords war
